text:
Predicates:
Adore(x, y) ::: x adores y.
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x is a design style of y.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Adore(max, x) ∧ DesignStyle(x, zaha) → InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (Adore(max, x) ∧ Brutalist(x) → ¬InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: No brutalist buildings that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (Adore(max, x) → (DesignStyle(x, zaha) ∨ DesignStyle(x, kelly))) ::: Every style that Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x (Adore(max, x) ∧ DesignStyle(x, kelly) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are evocative.
∀x (Adore(max, x) ∧ DesignStyle(x, kelly) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are dreamy.
∀x (Adore(max, x) ∧ InterestingGeometries(x) → (Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max that he adores has interesting geometries, then the design is a brutalist building and evocative.
Conclusion:
∃x (Adore(max, x) ∧ Brutalist(x)) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
